The c3 EXP-330 patch named the failure mode 'direct parameter import with form-substitution.' That argument is unchanged in c4 and survives adversarial review. Verdict (Self-Contradicted) holds.

holes_found.description: tldr_evidence currently reads: "The 23.45° is a globe parameter being incorporated from into a dome equation." The phrase 'incorporated from into' is grammatically broken (dangling 'from' with no object). Reader-facing TLDRs are what most non-expanding readers see first; broken English in the TLDR erodes the credibility of the review's rigor. Provenance traced: ISS-2281 ('HOL-TONE c2 hole 2: WIN-056 tldr_evidence uses "smuggled" — adversarial loaded verb', closed 2026-05-30T02:48:43Z, fixed_by decider-self-apply) replaced 'smuggled into' with 'incorporated from into' as a tone-softening patch. The closure verification_pattern was `grep -qF "incorporated from"` — a string-presence check that passes on the broken phrase. The grammar error was never caught because the verification gate had no grammaticality assertion. The c3 review (2026-05-14) predates ISS-2281 (2026-05-30), so this regression slipped between cycles.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'being incorporated from into a dome equation' with one of: (a) 'being incorporated into a dome equation' (drop dangling 'from'), (b) 'being imported from the globe into a dome equation' (supply the missing object — preserves the from↔into pair and reinforces the rival-model provenance message), or (c) 'being borrowed from the globe and dropped into a dome equation' (sharpest restatement of the c3 'direct parameter import with form-substitution' framing). Option (b) is preferred — it both fixes grammar and tightens the rhetoric without reintroducing 'smuggled.' Also: tighten the ISS-2281-class verification pattern. A literal grep-for-the-replacement-string passes too easily; either grep for the absence of the OLD phrase (`grep -qvF 'smuggled into'`) or include a tldr-readability check (e.g., Node natural-language pipeline that flags adjacent prepositions like 'from into').
holes_found.severity_rationale: TLDR is reader-facing and the broken phrase is in the user-visible Evidence summary that renders before the click-to-expand detail. Per curmudgeon.md TLDR severity rule: 'TLDR factual errors are major (readers see TLDRs first).' Grammatical breakage that produces a clearly malformed sentence is the same category as factual error from a reader-perception standpoint — both undermine the review's air of meticulousness. Not 'critical' because the underlying argument (23.45° is a globe parameter) survives the malformed sentence; not 'minor' because the breakage is unambiguous, not a stylistic preference.

WIN-044 (FSF) attacks version-instability of HAD/BOU values across V50.6 vs V51; WIN-056 (solar elevation) attacks formula-import-without-derivation; WIN-067 (Antarctic gravity hole) attacks the implied gravity drop under monotonic g↔H(r) coupling. advocate_mode.best_defense: A capable dome defender accepts our six methodological principles and replies: 'You concede H(r) is sophisticated curve-fitting that unifies three independent firmament measurements. Grant me one further posit — that the local sun's orbital path within the cavity is constrained by H(r) itself (the sun travels along the H(r) surface or at fixed altitude below it). Then a sinusoidal annual elevation modulation is not borrowed from the globe; it is the projection of an inclined annual orbit onto the H(r)-defined ceiling, with the inclination angle determined by the dome's own geometry. The numerical coincidence with the globe's 23.45° is then evidence FOR the dome, not against it — both models describe the same observed sun motion, and the dome offers a generative mechanism (H(r)-constrained sun orbit) where the globe offers only a kinematic description (axial tilt). Your text demands a derivation but does not show that no such derivation is possible — only that the dome author has not published one. Absence of publication is not impossibility.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Already preempted in current text ('The dome could close the loop by specifying sun motion within the cavity, deriving the resulting elevation-vs-latitude curve from dome parameters alone, and computing the sinusoidal amplitude (if any) without reference to 23.45°.'). The defense survives only at the meta level (the dome COULD in principle derive it) and our text already shifts the burden of proof appropriately. The defense does NOT close the gap that the dome AS PUBLISHED imports 23.45° verbatim. Defense rated 2/5 because it requires the dome to do work it has not done, and our text already names that requirement. No additional preemptive text needed.

deeper_analysis:
This c4 was triggered by drift-audit.json's flagging of WIN-056 (claim_length 7.4% drift) on 2026-06-18. The audit-flagged drift is partly a c3 fingerprint-record artifact (c3 wrote claim_length=27 for a 25-char string), but the re-review uncovered a real major hole the audit could not see: ISS-2281's tone fix landed grammatically broken text into a reader-facing TLDR, and the closure verification (grep for 'incorporated from') was too narrow to catch it. This is a useful natural experiment for the verification-pattern discipline: a string-presence check is necessary-but-insufficient when the patch is a tone or readability edit. A patch that substitutes one phrase for another should at minimum (a) assert ABSENCE of the old phrase AND (b) assert PRESENCE of the new phrase, AND ideally (c) include a readability/grammaticality smoke test on the affected field. Tinker may want to track this as a class of audit-gap rather than a per-issue fix. The decider's M2 / verify-pending architecture is the natural home for that check.

The c3 EXP-330 argument is intact and remains the strongest dome takedown in the WIN-044/056/067 cluster — its 'direct parameter import with form-substitution' framing crisply distinguishes WIN-056's failure mode from WIN-044's version-instability and WIN-067's gravity-implication-chain attacks. Lens-A advocate mode found one defensible-but-weak rebuttal (the 'sun orbit constrained by H(r)' posit), already preempted by the existing 'The dome could close the loop...' burden-shift sentence. Lens-C arithmetic confirms the arctan vs sinusoid contrast. Lens-B cross-WIN check is clean.
